observations.note: Output-level watermarking is broadly covered: green-list/KGW and variants, distortion-free and undetectable schemes, ECC multi-bit, learned/end-to-end, semantic and entropy-adaptive watermarks, post-hoc black-box schemes, certified robustness, WaterBench/WaterJudge.

Attack landscape covered: paraphrase/translation scrubbing, watermark stealing and spoofing, radioactivity/distillation, inhibitory attacks on backdoor fingerprints, dummy-neuron erasure, speculative-sampling trade-off.

Model fingerprinting is thinner than the topic warrants: instructional fingerprinting, Chain & Hash, AWM, EmbMarker, Hide-and-Seek appear, but other fingerprint families (e.g. representation/query-based fingerprints, merge-robust fingerprints) are absent and HuRef is only named.

Multimodal, code and audio watermarking is in the outline but the subsection itself states none of its technical claims are supported; code watermarking and multimodal coverage are effectively hollow.

Training-data / dataset watermarking and data-provenance for copyright, a key part of LLM provenance, appears only incidentally (benchmark-contamination watermarking; a data-watermark paper named only inside leaked notes).
Peripheral governance topics (EU AI Act, NIST RMF, forensic admissibility, equity, dual use) are present.

anchor_justification: Most central areas are present, but several key points are missing or only named (data watermarking, fingerprinting breadth, multimodal/code, deployed schemes like SynthID only mentioned). This matches 3 ('generally comprehensive ... misses a few key points'); 4 requires that only very minor topics are left out, which does not hold.

observations.note: Macro-outline is logical: taxonomy -> output-level -> model-centric -> attacks -> evaluation -> governance, with explicit forward/backward transitions between subsections.
About 850 words of leaked citation-verification notes ('Thus, the corrected subsection contains no citations') sit in the body, followed by a second full version of the subsection's paragraph.
Draft with inline 'must be removed / is correct and retained' notes, then '**Corrected subsection with only valid citations**' and a second version; the same subsection appears twice.
'Parameter-space watermarking' subsection discusses output-level/decoding methods (MPAC, WaterMod, Permute-and-Flip, CATER) already treated in 3.2/3.4; category boundaries not respected.
Threat-model taxonomy proposed twice with overlapping axes and examples; evaluation 'myopia' framing opens both 3.5 and 6.1; longitudinal-gap point restated in about seven places.
4.5 citations collapse to [86] including the survey's own title; conclusion opens with 'This subsection synthesizes', a generation artifact.

anchor_justification: The skeleton would support a 3, but anchor 2's 'some content arranged in a disordered or unreasonable manner' literally holds for 7.1, 7.5, 4.4 and 4.5, beyond the 'links and transitions could be improved' of level 3. The survey sits between 2 and 3, so the lower level is chosen.

observations.note: Introduction and taxonomy are tightly about LLM watermarking/fingerprinting and distinguish them from safety, privacy and alignment.
Technical chapters stay on watermarking and fingerprinting methods and attacks.
Large blocks of reader-visible meta-commentary about which citations are in 'the provided list' are not content about the topic.
Digressions into universal jailbreak suffixes and MLLM backdoor attacks (BadToken, AnyDoor) that are not watermark or fingerprint attacks.

Tangents to RAG risk frameworks, ZKP privacy proposals and generic surveillance concerns; many statements are attached to papers about other things (e.g. lexical-substitution paper credited with Thinking/Answering phase separation in 6.3).

anchor_justification: Generally on topic with some unrelated material, which is level 3. Level 4 requires infrequent digressions; the ~1,500 words of leaked notes plus scattered off-topic attacks and misattributed content are more than infrequent.

observations.note: Explicit framework of embedding locus x detection modality x security properties x threat axes, with the axes cross-mapped to each other (e.g. modality spectrum mapped to adversary capability).
Identifies a recurring asymmetry across studies (detection needs significance, spoofing/removal needs mimicry) and reframes radioactivity as an attack surface: real cross-study patterns.
Contrasts empirical semantic robustness with formal certificates (smoothing/ECC); positions backdoor watermarking vs behavior-space fingerprints by access condition.

The headline convergence thesis rests on misattributed descriptions (Chain & Hash fusing 'latent-space confusion zones', PLMmark embedding ZKPs in MPC, ECC papers combining 'acrostic constraints'); such connections do not count as synthesis.
Many links are rhetorical cross-references ('directly echoing', 'foreshadowing') and the same synthesized point is repeated rather than developed.

anchor_justification: Some thematic relationships are real (level 3). Level 4 needs most studies integrated into coherent themes or debates; here the integrating framework is declared more than demonstrated and its key links are unreliable, so the survey sits between 3 and 4 and gets 3.

observations.note: States concrete paradigm limits: output-space signals not radioactive, parameter-space needs white-box access, spectral fingerprints degrade below INT4.
Reasoned critique of robustness evaluation: synthetic token edits vs human paraphrasing, missing composite attacks, longitudinal blindness, inadequacy of BLEU/perplexity.
Argues formal security for model-centric schemes is 'largely aspirational' because guarantees assume white-box access and static models.
Inconsistent critique: 3.2 says rejection sampling 'resolves' the 'Watermarks in the Sand' impossibility, which 2.3 and 5.4 present as a general limit.
Individual studies are mostly reported with success figures rather than critiqued; limitations are often assigned to the wrong papers.
Critique is repetitive (longitudinal gap ~7 times, RTT 88%->13% figure ~6 times) and many subsections end in generic 'future work must' statements.

anchor_justification: Critique exists and is sometimes specific (5.6, 4.5) but is applied to paradigms rather than most key studies, and is inconsistent. This fits 3; level 4 requires systematic critique of most key studies.
